bc_arrow_lake.blurb: Arrow Lake is a bouldering-focused stretch of the West Kootenay in British Columbia, near Castlegar, spread out along the shore of the lake. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with problems from the easiest grades up through V9, and the bulk of them landing between V1 and V5. Sport routes, mostly 5.10 and 5.11, and a smaller helping of trad sit on cliffs above. The stone is compact gneiss with plenty of features, and it is mostly clean. Several slopes face south and soak up the sun, while some zones stay shady, and the season stretches roughly eight to nine months, generally dry from March into November. Fantasyland, Keenlyside and Syringa are among the largest zones, and Fantasyland packs its boulders onto a bench with views over the water.

ut_rock_canyon.blurb: Rock Canyon cuts into the Wasatch Range right beside Provo, Utah, and holds close to five hundred climbs. Sport routes dominate, backed by a sizable trad selection and a handful of boulders. Grades run mostly from 5.7 to 5.12, centered on 5.10 and 5.11, so there are moderates as well as plenty for stronger climbers. The walls are quartzite and limestone, and the quartzite gives a blend of small edges and bigger jug holds. Climbing is possible all year, though June through October tends to bring the steadiest weather and driest rock. Sub-areas include the Galaxy Area, the Mouth Boulders and the Ed and Terry Wall.

ca_new_jack_city.blurb: New Jack City sits in the high desert near Barstow, California, at roughly 3,700 feet, and is sport climbing almost through and through, with a few top-ropes, trad lines and a small bouldering section. Grades span from easy to 5.13, but the weight sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a fair number of moderates from 5.6 to 5.9. The rock is a metamorphic stone of volcanic origin, and the climbing is steep and varied: pockets, huecos, edges, jugs and crimps, with sequences that reward both strength and technique. The season generally runs October through May. Box Canyon East is the busiest sector with the most routes, followed by the Entrance Area Crags and Box Canyon West.

nb_welsford.blurb: Welsford lies in southern New Brunswick, within reach of both Saint John and Fredericton, and holds a handful of crags. Traditional climbing leads by a wide margin, with a solid bolted minority and a few top-ropes. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.12, with 5.10 the busiest grade and enough moderates to suit newer leaders. Cochrane Lane Cliffs, the largest by far, are pink granite. Sunnyside is different: diabase, bolted, with jugs, crimps and slopes. Mount Douglas offers slabs with good protection, while Eagle Rock has newer trad lines. There is also a small boulder area, and ice climbing is on offer too.

va_dc_northern_va_region.blurb: This region gathers the climbing around Washington, DC and northern Virginia into many small pockets plus one major crag. Bouldering is the biggest share, followed by trad and top-rope, with only a sliver of sport. Boulder problems mostly sit between V0 and V4, and the roped routes run mostly 5.7 to 5.11. Great Falls, on the Potomac in Mather Gorge, is the heart of the roped climbing: short routes of about 20 to 60 feet, mostly face climbing on slick mica schist, where top-roping is the usual approach and natural protection is scarce. Many climbs sit along the river in a rugged gorge setting. Smaller boulder spots such as Springfield Bouldering, Cross Country Trail Boulders and Alum Springs fill out the rest.

ca_donner_truckee_bouldering.blurb: Donner/Truckee Bouldering covers granite boulders scattered along the Interstate 80 corridor in the northern Sierra, all within about half an hour of Truckee. Almost every climb is a boulder problem, with a wide spread of grades: plenty of V0 to V5 for moderate climbers, and a tail of hard problems up to V11. The granite is high quality, and at Castle Peak it is compact and featured, spread over southwest-facing hillsides and meadows in more than a dozen clusters. Summit Lake offers scattered boulders in an alpine setting. At this elevation snow cover and aspect decide what is climbable, so conditions vary by zone. Castle Peak, Donner Memorial State Park, Yuba Gap and Donner Pass hold the most problems.
